description.value: The study examined whether cerebellar activity during visual motion perception reflects sustained attention to salient motion or the detection and discrimination of motion under high perceptual uncertainty.

spans.text: Here, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging to determine the degree to which cerebellar involvement in visual motion perception can be explained by a role in sustained attentive tracking of moving stimuli in contrast to a role in visual motion discrimination.

design.value: An event-related fMRI study manipulated attention by directing participants to attend covertly either to random-dot motion or to a colored fixation spot, and manipulated perceptual uncertainty by varying motion coherence.

spans.text: While holding the visual displays constant, we manipulated attention by having participants attend covertly to a field of random-dot motion or a colored spot at fixation.
